IE.q: A client wants to run a prize draw using their newsletter list. Is consent still valid?
IE.a: No. Consent obtained for newsletter delivery does not extend to a prize draw — the new purpose is incompatible with the one disclosed at collection, and the DPC treats re-purposing of marketing lists as a separate processing operation requiring fresh, specific consent.

cites.text: Consent must be specific to each purpose (§ 56)

FR.q: A client wants to run a prize draw using their newsletter list. Is consent still valid?
FR.a: No. The CNIL's position is stricter than the baseline: prospection for a distinct operation requires its own opt-in, and the collection notice must name the promotional purpose. Re-use of an existing list exposes the client to a sanction under Article 82 of the Loi Informatique et Libertés.

DE.q: A client wants to run a prize draw using their newsletter list. Is consent still valid?
DE.a: No, and there is an additional national dimension: the coupling prohibition under § 7 UWG plus BGH case law on Kopplungsverbot mean the draw cannot be conditioned on marketing consent. A separate, documented opt-in is required and must be logged with its timestamp.

NL.q: A client wants to run a prize draw using their newsletter list. Is consent still valid?
NL.a: No. The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens requires purpose-specific consent, and the Telecommunicatiewet soft opt-in for existing customers does not cover promotional draws. Document the new consent and retain the withdrawal mechanism in the same record.

ES.q: A client wants to run a prize draw using their newsletter list. Is consent still valid?
ES.a: No. The AEPD requires consent granular to each purpose, and LSSI Article 21 governs the electronic communication itself. Prize-draw terms must also disclose the retention period for entrant data separately from the newsletter retention rule.
